title: EKS Terraform upgrade-simulator module + health-gate runbook
creator: Asha Patel
description: Build a reusable Terraform module and supporting test harness that can execute a simulated control-plane upgrade path for Redwood Private EKS clusters. The simulator will run Terraform plan/apply against an ephemeral sandbox (mock or throwaway cluster) to validate changes, exercise upgrade hooks, and produce health-gate metrics that the Console can use for safe rollouts.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable Terraform module published under modules/eks-upgrade-sim that provisions an ephemeral EKS cluster and samba of required infra for testing upgrades
An automation pipeline (GitHub Actions + Terratest wrapper) that performs a dry-run & a simulated in-place upgrade and emits a standardized JSON health report
Health-gate schema defined (latency, API error spike, kube-controller restart rate, etc.) and integrated with Console feature flags/rollout API
A rollback playbook and automated rollback trigger mock that can be invoked when a health-gate threshold is breached
Documentation and runbook in Confluence plus a reference PR linking the module and pipeline
tasks: Design health-gate metric set and thresholds (PM + SRE)
Implement Terraform module: cluster, nodegroups, control-plane hooks, test IAM roles
Write Terratest suites for idempotence and simulated drift then run against sandbox accounts
Create GH Actions workflow to orchestrate simulate-upgrade -> collect métrics -> post report to Console staging endpoint
Add telemetry export: CloudWatch -> metrics-lambda -> Console dev tracer for visualization
Author rollback playbook and automation to apply rollback TF state or call Canary fallback route
progress_updates: 2026-01-20: Kickoff meeting with SRE and PM. Agreed on minimal metric set: API latency p95, apiserver 5xx rate, controller-manager restarts/min, cluster-autoscaler events.
2026-01-27: Module skeleton checked in (modules/eks-upgrade-sim). Created base variables and outputs. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2317
2026-02-03: Early Terratest harness added to run 'terraform init/plan/apply' against a disposable account using account-stubs. Wrote smoke assertions for nodegroup readiness.
2026-02-12: Prototype health-reporter lambda implemented. Emits health JSON to staging Console endpoint: https://console-staging.redwood.ai/rollouts/health-reports
2026-02-18: Ran first simulated upgrade against sandbox-qa-3: observed transient controller-manager restart spike. Added a stabilization window in the pipeline and tuned thresholds.

2026-02-24: Open design questions: whether to simulate upgrades by applying exact upstream control-plane changes (kubelet/user-AMI) versus forcing rollout via Kubernetes API. SRE prefers API-driven hairpin to avoid cross-account runtime differences. Added follow-up task to validate both approaches.
2026-02-25: Draft runbook created in Confluence and linked below. Preparing PR for review (integration tests flaky under cost constraints; need dedicated sandbox budget approval).
notes: This module intentionally creates ephemeral infra in sandbox accounts; coordinate with FinOps for cost caps. Consider flagging heavy runs behind a feature flag to avoid accidental billing. For security review: IAM roles created in sandbox must follow least privilege and have an expiration TTL.
review_feedback: PM (Linnea Sørensen): Add a column to the health report for severity and suggested corrective action
SRE (Kim Chen): Prefer API-driven upgrade simulation for faster iteration; allow a secondary 'full-controlplane-recreate' mode for longer, higher-fidelity tests
Design (Marta Ruiz): Make sure module exposes variables for KMS key ARN and CNI plugin variant to match customer configurations
next_steps: Address PR feedback and land module base (owner: Diego)
Request sandbox budget for extended runs (owner: Asha)
Implement optional 'recreate' mode and compare signals from both simulation strategies (owner: SRE team)
Wire health-report output to Console rollout gating API and add sample dashboard in Console staging
